tools.name: list_devices
tools.title: List Android devices
tools.description: List connected Android devices with model, Android version, and SDK level. Use the serial in other tools when multiple devices are connected. Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

tools.name: get_state
tools.title: Get device and app state
tools.description: Returns the connected device, screen size/density/orientation, foreground package and activity, process ids, and the app's ViewRootImpl windows (if debuggable). Call this before UI inspection to learn what is on screen. Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

serial.description: Device serial; omit when only one device is connected.

package.description: Package to inspect; defaults to the foreground app.

tools.name: dump_ui
tools.title: Dump the UI hierarchy
tools.description: Capture the current UI. source=view uses the ViewDebug hierarchy over JDWP (full View classes, layout params, padding, visibility, margins; requires a debuggable app). source=semantics uses the accessibility tree via uiautomator (best zero-config option for Compose text/elements; works on any app). source=compose uses Android Studio's transport/JVMTI Compose inspector to return composable names, file/line, bounds, parameters/text and recomposition counts (requires a debuggable app, a local Android Studio install, and Compose 1.8.3 by default). auto selects semantics for Compose apps and view otherwise. format=tree renders a readable tree, format=json (default) returns the full structured tree, format=compact drops nodes with no text/content description/interaction/state and promotes their children, and format=flat emits those same nodes in pre-order with depth. settle=true waits for the app to stop producing frames and reports stability, so an animation or a loading spinner cannot silently produce a wrong snapshot. window=all captures every window of the app (dialogs, popups, separate ViewRootImpls) and returns them under view.windows instead of a single view.roots. Nodes include ref, bounds, visibleBounds, center, clickable and the full parent path is available in find_elements. Use this for requests such as "抓取当前页面布局", "导出布局树", "当前界面有什么", or "dump the screen": call get_state first, then dump_ui(source="auto", format="tree"). Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

package.description: Package to inspect; defaults to foreground app.

source.description: auto (default), view, semantics, dumpsys, compose, or both.

format.description: json (default, full tree), tree (readable), compact (content/interactive nodes only, children promoted), or flat (compact in pre-order with depth).

depth.description: Limit JSON/compact tree depth; omit for full depth.

includeProperties.description: Include every ViewDebug property in JSON.

settle.description: Wait for the UI to stop animating before capturing and report stability.

window.description: ViewRootImpl window to capture for source=view: a 0-based index, a name substring, or "all" for every window of the app.

savePath.description: Write the full JSON dump to this file.

tools.name: find_elements
tools.title: Find elements
tools.description: Search the current UI tree by text, content description, resource id, class, or node ref. Defaults to a case-insensitive contains match. Returns bounds, center, clickable state, and the full path for each match. This is the best way to locate an element and get its device coordinates. Use this when the user points at a visible element ("看下当前“登录”按钮", "这个控件多大/在哪/可点击吗", "顶部那个图标是什么"); the result includes bounds, center, clickable, enabled, and className. Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

query.description: Text, id, class, ref, or regex to search for.

match.description: Match mode (default contains; /regex/ syntax is also accepted).

both.description: Search both view and semantics trees (default: primary tree only).

window.description: View window to search (index or name substring from get_state); default is the focused window.

tools.name: locate_code
tools.title: Locate code behind a UI element
tools.description: Scan the current Android repository for the source of a UI element. Pass the anchors returned by dump_ui/find_elements: visible text, content description, resource id, Compose name/file/line, or View class. Returns string-resource/layout/Compose anchors plus ranked candidates with file, line, kind, score, reason and a snippet. This is the deterministic step before reading code; it is read-only and does not modify the repository. Use the returned anchors and candidates to open files and trace the click/state chain. Use only when the user references a visible UI element on the current screen or asks where UI code is implemented; not for general Android concept questions, code review, or performance debugging. Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit Android/device request.

root.description: Repository root (default: the MCP server's working directory).

id.description: Resource ids, with or without package prefix; repeatable.

composeFile.description: File name/path reported by the Compose inspector.

composeLine.description: Line reported by the Compose inspector.

includeTests.description: Include test sources in the ranking.

tools.name: hit_test
tools.title: Hit-test a screen point
tools.description: Return the element(s) at a screen coordinate. Matching mirrors LayoutInspectorV2-Pro: all nodes containing the point are sorted by smallest area, with deeper/later-drawn nodes winning ties. By default both the view and semantics trees are queried, so you get the View class and the Compose/accessibility node for the same point. Set source=compose to hit-test the JVMTI Compose tree instead. Use index to cycle through overlapping candidates. Use for "屏幕坐标 300,800 是什么" and "what is at x,y"; returns all overlapping candidates by index. Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

window.description: View window to hit-test (index or name substring); default is the focused window.

tools.name: analyze_ui
tools.title: Analyze layout issues
tools.description: Run layout/accessibility checks over the current UI: tiny touch targets (<48dp by default), overlapping sibling clickables, clipped or offscreen nodes, invisible clickables, unlabeled clickables, duplicate resource ids, deep nesting, and nodes extending outside their parent. Use this after making a UI change to catch regressions. Also answers "有没有小点击区域", "有没有重叠", "无障碍检查", "布局有没有问题", and "有没有错位/被裁剪". Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

includeProperties.description: Capture raw View properties (default true); overdraw and rtl_issues need them. Pass false for a faster, smaller capture.

settle.description: Wait for the UI to stop animating before capturing and report stability.

tools.name: list_fragments
tools.title: List Activity and Fragment structure
tools.description: Report the Activity and Fragment structure of the foreground app from `dumpsys activity`: fragment class (or tag when the class is obfuscated), lifecycle state, and whether it is added/hidden/detached. Works on non-debuggable apps, where the ViewDebug source fails. Framework bookkeeping fragments (AndroidX ReportFragment, LifecycleDispatcher tags) are filtered out. Use this to answer "which Fragment implements this page" before scanning source. It returns no view hierarchy; pair it with dump_ui(source="dumpsys") for nodes. Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

package.description: Package to inspect; defaults to the foreground app.

includeFramework.description: Keep AndroidX lifecycle bookkeeping fragments (ReportFragment etc.).

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Take a screenshot
tools.description: Capture the device screen as a PNG and return it as image content. This is also the final fallback when structured UI capture fails. By default the image is downscaled to 720px wide to keep responses small; pass fullResolution=true for the native resolution, or maxWidth/scale for a custom size. The text metadata always includes originalWidth/originalHeight, screenWidth/screenHeight, and coordinateMapping.imageToDevice so you can map vision coordinates back to device coordinates before reporting a position. Optionally save the PNG and generate an SVG overlay with node boxes (annotatedPath). Use for "截个图看看" and "看一下画面". A screenshot cannot reliably reveal text color or font size; do not infer style from pixels. Android repos only; non-Android: call only on an explicit device/screen request or Android mention.

annotate.description: Also write an .annotated.svg with node boxes next to savePath.

maxWidth.description: Downscale to at most this width (default 720).

scale.description: Downscale by this factor (alternative to maxWidth).

fullResolution.description: Return the native resolution instead of the default 720px width.
